plans.what_the_keep_going_behaviour_becomes:
Unchanged in substance, and unchanged in code at the open site. rollbackFailure still records "open rollback root: <err>" and still walks every target with a nil handle. What changes is only the one branch that used to die: a private untracked target with a recorded publication now gets the error "rollback root is unavailable; private target left as published: <path>" appended to rollback.Errors, and the loop continues to the next target. Everything after it still runs: the dirty-tracked branch still runs git restore --staged before its own guard, the existing-untracked branch still runs git rm --cached and its unrooted restore, the tracked branch still restores from HEAD, the created-paths loop still runs git rm --cached, and the final index check still runs. The result is what the open-site decision exists to produce: Rollback.Status = RollbackIncomplete, Outcome = OutcomeRisk, Failure.Kind = FailureRollback, with both the open failure and the unrestored target named. Observed in the prototype: errors = ["open rollback root: open /tmp/.../001: no such file or directory", "rollback root is unavailable; private target left as published: memory/logs/created.md", "inspect Git index: exit status 128"] (the third is the fixture killing git, see honest_downsides). Under the execute-only fixture as uid 65534, where git survives, the errors were exactly the first two and the index check passed, so the unstage half of keep-going is intact.

What the guard does NOT do, on purpose: it does not fall back to unrooted os.Rename/os.WriteFile to quarantine or restore. The rooted handle exists to close symlink-escape races during rollback; an unrooted fallback would reopen them at the worst moment. So with no handle, the published bytes stay at the path and, if the target existed before the transaction, its preimage (held only in memory in state.originalBytes) is not written back. The message says "left as published" so the operator knows which state the file is in.
plans.the_no_handle_test:
Name: TestRollbackWithoutRootHandleReportsPrivateTargetLeftAsPublished, in git_transaction_test.go.

Mechanism (chosen): rename the worktree root away from inside the mutation callback, after the last successful open. Fixture: newRepository, mkdir memory/logs, one target "memory/logs/created.md" declared in both TargetPaths and PrivateUntrackedTargetPaths. Callback: RecordCreated, os.WriteFile("ours\n", 0o600), RecordPublished (this is the last os.OpenRoot that must succeed, at line 370), then os.Rename(repositoryRoot, repositoryRoot+"-renamed-away"), then return errors.New("force rollback"). ExecuteTransaction goes straight from the mutation error to rollbackFailure (lines 584-586) with no root use in between, so the rollback open at line 994 is the only open that fails, with ENOENT. The test renames the directory back, then asserts: Outcome == OutcomeRisk, Rollback.Status == RollbackIncomplete, Failure.Kind == FailureRollback; one rollback error has prefix "open rollback root: " and one contains both "rollback root is unavailable" and the target path; the file still holds "ours\n" (left as published, neither quarantined nor deleted); no ".do-work-private-rollback-*" directory exists in the root (nothing rooted ran). Renaming a numbered t.TempDir() subdirectory inside its per-test parent is safe: the parent is removed whole at cleanup.

Privileges: none. It runs as uid 0, which is what this session is (id -u = 0), and as an unprivileged uid.

Proof in the scratch clone (all outputs verbatim in this session):
- At HEAD 494a4ae, unguarded, as uid 0: the test panics: "runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference" at os.(*Root).Mkdir <- quarantineAndRollbackPrivate git_transaction.go:1213 <- rollbackFailure :1032 <- ExecuteTransaction :586. Exit 1. That is the REQ's RED case reproduced through the public API.
- With the guard: --- PASS (0.04s); package suite ok 2.724s; lock-in "Audit lock-in regressions passed".
- Guard ablated again on the final tree (private copy req598-ablate2): same panic at :1213 via :1032, exit 1; lock-in "FAIL: 8 nil-root guards ... REQ-598 pinned exactly 9". So the floor now has a behavioural witness, not only a count.
- REQ-558's reproduce command on the final tree prints 9 sites and lists git_transaction_test.go; the "NO TEST covers any nil-root branch" line is gone.

Alternatives, each tried or read, and why not shipped:
- Execute-only root (chmod 0111), the mechanism REQ-558's F3 named. Proven: os.OpenRoot opens O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC (GOROOT/src/os/root_unix.go openRootNolog), so it needs read permission and fails with EACCES for a non-root uid, while git -C needs only search permission. Run as uid 65534 via setpriv on a compiled test binary: unguarded -> the same panic at :1213; guarded -> PASS, with "os.OpenRoot ...: permission denied", "git -C ... rev-parse --show-toplevel" succeeding, and the tail index check producing no error, so this fixture shows BOTH halves of keep-going. But uid 0 bypasses directory permission checks: as root the open succeeds and the test must t.Skip (verified: "--- SKIP" as uid 0). This machine and its gate run as uid 0, so the package's "first no-handle test" would never execute here. Not shipped; the rename fixture is.
- A regular file at the root path: newRoot fstat-rejects non-directories ("not a directory"), also privilege-free, but it needs the rename anyway plus a file write; strictly more moving parts than the rename alone.
- A seam (var openRollbackRoot = os.OpenRoot swapped by the test): deterministic, privilege-free, git survives, and house-legal (privateTransactionTestHook is the precedent), but it adds production code whose only caller is a test and never exercises the real syscall failure. Rejected under delete-before-add; the real ENOENT does the job.

honest_downsides: Nine per-consumer checks remain, and the design smell REQ-558 named stands: the handle's nil-ness is still decided eleven times downstream instead of once at the open. privateStateStillOriginal and rootedCreateRegular still dereference the handle without testing it and are safe only because guards at their call sites stand in front of them.

What a future consumer of the handle has to remember, with nothing in the code to remind it: write its own nil branch choosing the conservative answer for its target; move the pin (that part is loud, the ceiling trips); add a case to the no-handle test if its path differs from the private-untracked one (that part is silent if forgotten, and so is the missing guard itself).

The new guard creates one more doubly-checked pair, rollbackDirtyTracked (its own guard at 1176) -> quarantineAndRollbackPrivate (the new one), which is exactly the redundancy class the audit that produced REQ-558 counted as a finding.

Two message shapes for one condition: rollbackDirtyTracked returns the bare 'rollback root is unavailable' with no path; the new guard names the target. The sibling was left alone to keep the change minimal, so the inconsistency is introduced here, not inherited.

The shipped fixture kills git along with the open (ENOENT on the root), so the test proves the reporting half of keep-going and cannot prove the unstage half; that half rests on unchanged code and on a planning-session run as uid 65534 that does not ship. A test that shows both halves exists (execute-only root) but would skip on every uid-0 machine, this one included, so shipping it would add a test that never runs here.

With no handle, a private target that existed before the transaction keeps the published bytes and loses its on-disk preimage; the guard reports that state rather than restoring through unrooted writes. That is a deliberate non-fix, and the single message does not distinguish a created target from a pre-existing one.

The fixture's real-world story is a worktree root that disappears mid-transaction, which is a rarer cause of a failed open than a permission change; the branch it drives is the same either way, but the fixture reads as odd next to the sibling tests.
The Finding 3 block in the lock-in grows by seven comment lines; the count it pins is still blind to a guard rewritten as a helper call, as its own comment already says.

plans.shape:
Shipped shape: (a) — decide the handle once at the open in rollbackFailure. When openRollbackRoot (= os.OpenRoot) fails, record the one open error, run rollbackWithoutRoot (the half that needs no handle: every Git-side unstage and restore-from-HEAD, plus the plain-path restore of existing untracked targets) and report every target the rooted half would have touched as "left in place; rollback root is unavailable". When it succeeds, run rollbackWithRoot, which is today's three loops verbatim minus the eight nil tests, under a handle that is non-nil by construction. All eight guards become dead and are deleted in this change; the ninth, missing one is subsumed because quarantineAndRollbackPrivate is now only reachable from rollbackWithRoot.

(b) was designed and rejected in both forms. Pure (b) — hand rollbackFailure the *os.Root ExecuteTransaction already holds from its line-467 open (still open at all ten call sites) and delete the reopen — is the smallest diff of all, but it makes the fixed requirement unwritable: there is no longer any no-handle rollback to test ("open forced to fail" now means ExecuteTransaction refuses before mutating), and it changes which directory object rollback acts on if the worktree root is swapped mid-transaction. Hybrid (b) — fresh open, fall back to the caller's handle on failure — reports a rollback that fully completed as RollbackIncomplete (the open error is in Errors) or needs a new result category, and its only real wins are ENOENT/EMFILE cases where `git -C` is failing anyway. A third variant (a null-object interface whose methods return a typed error, replacing *os.Root in nine signatures) was considered and rejected: it keeps the loops untouched but preserves messages that describe filesystem observations nobody made.

Prototyped and verified in a clone: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-do-work/213e30ac-5958-56c8-9fd2-faaaaf9c4ea6/scratchpad/req598-decide-once (NOT the given path req598 — see honest_downsides: that path turned out to be shared with the sibling plan's live edits).

plans.what_the_keep_going_behaviour_becomes:
It survives in substance, by construction rather than by eight scattered checks: a failed open still leaves nothing staged and still returns the same typed result (Rollback.Status = incomplete, Failure.Kind = rollback_incomplete, Outcome = committed_state_risk, first error "open rollback root: <PathError>"). What rollbackWithoutRoot does per kind, against what today's nil-handle path did:

- Dirty-tracked opt-in: `git restore --staged` (same). Then "dirty tracked target left in place; rollback root is unavailable: <path>" in place of today's "was not identity-recorded" / "rollback root is unavailable".
- Private untracked: "private target left in place; rollback root is unavailable: <path>" in place of today's "was not identity-recorded" (unrecorded) or the panic (recorded).
- Existing untracked opt-in: restoreExistingUntracked runs in full — unchanged; it never needed the handle.
- Tracked: targetIsDirty; if not dirty, skip; if the publication is unrecorded, `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree` and action "restored <path> from HEAD" — unchanged; if recorded, `git restore --staged` then "tracked target left in place; rollback root is unavailable: <path>" instead of today's misleading "changed after publication; preserved replacement".
- Created paths: skip those owned by the target loop, `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` (same), then "created target left in place; rollback root is unavailable: <path>" instead of "preserved replacement"/"not identity-recorded; preserved object".
- Created directories: "created directory left in place; rollback root is unavailable: <path>" instead of "was not identity-recorded".
- Loop 4 unchanged, so "the declared target paths are still staged after rollback" still fires if any unstage was missed.

Proof it survives after the change: the shipped test forces the open to fail through ExecuteTransaction with a mutated tracked file, an identity-recorded private target and a staged created path, and observes Actions == ["restored tracked.txt from HEAD"], `git ls-files created.txt` empty, Errors exactly [open error, private left in place, created left in place] (so the "still staged" line did not fire), tracked.txt back at HEAD bytes, the private and created files untouched, no quarantine directory. A second, throwaway run of the sibling plan's forcing mechanism (rename the root away: open fails ENOENT and every `git -C` fails too) returned the same typed incomplete result with errors ["open rollback root: open …: no such file or directory", "private target left in place; …", "inspect Git index: exit status 128"] and no panic.

Nothing outside the .go files or do-work/ greps for the old no-handle wording (rg over the repo excluding *.go and do-work/: 0 files).
plans.the_no_handle_test:
TestRollbackWithoutRootHandleUnstagesRestoresFromHeadAndReportsTheRest, in git_transaction_test.go, driven through ExecuteTransaction.

Forcing mechanism: the seam. `openRollbackRoot = func(name string) (*os.Root, error) { return nil, &os.PathError{Op: "open", Path: name, Err: syscall.EACCES} }` with t.Cleanup restoring os.OpenRoot (use Op "open": that is what a real os.OpenRoot PathError carries — observed `open /tmp/…: no such file or directory`; my prototype used "openat" and should be corrected). Why not the two seam-free options: (1) chmod 0111 on the worktree root is the real condition (open fails, `git -C` works) but uid 0 bypasses it — verified here: OpenRoot on a 0111 directory returns a handle as root — so the test would skip in exactly the environment this suite runs in; (2) renaming the root away (the sibling plan's trick) is root-proof but kills every `git -C` along with the handle, so the Git-side half this design exists to keep is unobservable. The seam is the only mechanism under which the keep-going claim can be asserted, and it is the same pattern as privateTransactionTestHook. The package has no t.Parallel (it uses t.Setenv), so a package-level var is safe.

Fixture: newRepository; tracked.txt committed as "committed\n"; .git/info/exclude "/memory/logs/"; memory/logs/note.md written "old note\n" (existing, untracked, excluded → a private target with a preimage). Options: TargetPaths [tracked.txt, memory/logs/note.md, created.txt], PrivateUntrackedTargetPaths [memory/logs/note.md]. Mutation: RecordTouched(tracked.txt) + write "mutated\n"; RecordTouched(note.md) + write "new note\n" + RecordPublished(note.md) — the identity-recorded private target, the RED case; RecordCreated(created.txt) + write + RecordTouched + `git add -- created.txt` so the unstage is observable; return errors.New("force rollback").

Assertions: Outcome == OutcomeRisk, Failure.Kind == FailureRollback, Rollback.Status == RollbackIncomplete; Rollback.Errors deep-equal to exactly ["open rollback root: open <root>: permission denied", "private target left in place; rollback root is unavailable: memory/logs/note.md", "created target left in place; rollback root is unavailable: created.txt"] (exactness is deliberate: it proves the "still staged after rollback" line is absent, i.e. the unstage happened — states are sorted by normalizeTargetPaths so the order is stable); Rollback.Actions deep-equal ["restored tracked.txt from HEAD"]; tracked.txt reads "committed\n"; `git ls-files -- created.txt` is empty; created.txt still "created\n" and note.md still "new note\n" (left in place, reported, not touched); no directory named .do-work-private-rollback-* exists (nothing rooted ran).

Evidence: against HEAD plus the seam alone the test panics at quarantineAndRollbackPrivate(0x0, …) → root.Mkdir (RED); after the change it passes in 0.07s (GREEN). Separately, the real condition was reproduced once at HEAD through ExecuteTransaction with a throwaway probe compiled as root and run as uid 65534 with the root chmod'd 0111 from inside the mutation: the panic trace is ExecuteTransaction:586 → rollbackFailure:1032 → quarantineAndRollbackPrivate:1213 root.Mkdir. verdict.why:
Both plans close the panic and both RED/GREEN reproduce on current HEAD 75da24a (verified in fresh clones). They differ in what the package can prove afterwards and in what a future edit has to remember.

What A preserves: byte-identical code on every working path (+9/-4 in the source), no new production seam, a test that drives a real ENOENT. What A costs: nine per-consumer decisions stay, and nothing in the code reminds a tenth consumer to add its own; the no-handle path keeps messages that describe observations nobody made ("changed after created-object capture; preserved replacement" when the handle was simply missing, verified in my differential run at HEAD); and A's shipped test cannot show the keep-going half at all, because renaming the root kills every `git -C` along with the open (verified: the same fixture reports "inspect Git index: exit status 128"). The REQ says the test is the point as much as the fix, and A's test proves only the reporting half.

What B preserves: I could show it behaviour-preserving to my satisfaction, which was the condition for picking it. Handle-present half: the package suite is green with zero edits to existing tests, and a panic canary at the top of rollbackWithoutRoot never fires across the existing suite while the new test does fire it, so no existing test crossed into the new half and the moved loops are what the suite covered before. No-handle half: one fixture covering every kind that does not panic at HEAD, run under HEAD+seam and under B, gives identical outcome, status, actions, file bytes, `git status` and `git ls-files`; the only diff is error wording, and B's wording is the true one. The -U0 diff removes exactly the eight guard lines and adds none. What B costs: +155/-81 in a transaction boundary, a package-level test seam, and a second walk of the target kinds that must stay in step with the first. Those are real and are listed under honest_downsides.

Maintainer preference vs request preference: they only conflict if "simple" means "fewest lines". The maintainer's own words are that existing complexity is not evidence it should stay and that machinery is not an achievement. Eleven consumers each answering "is the handle usable" is that machinery, and REQ-558 showed the per-consumer pattern is how one of nine could be missing with every gate green. B deletes eight guards, the stale enumeration comment on rootedOpenSnapshot, and the misleading no-handle messages; it adds one decision and the Git-only walk that the keep-going contract needs anyway. The pin goes from "exactly 9" to "zero", which is a simpler invariant to hold. So the request's preference wins, and it wins on the maintainer's own terms, with the cost stated rather than hidden.

(6) The shipped test: RED at HEAD+seam (panic at root.Mkdir), GREEN after; also PASS as uid 65534.

Gate: full maintainer-verify on the B tree ran 1m46s; every lane green except the go-test budget lane, where the only red is internal/heavyverification (7 FAIL lines, all subtests of TestShippedRuntimeEvidenceTracksEffectiveGoSettingsAndBinaryBytes and TestShippedGitIsolationPreservesGenericLaneInheritance). Both plans report the same two red at clean HEAD; I did not re-run clean HEAD myself, so step 1 records that pair and step 5 compares against it.
risks: R1 Two walks that must stay in step: a new target kind or a new rooted consumer added to rollbackWithRoot without a counterpart in rollbackWithoutRoot loses the no-handle handling for that kind silently (no panic, no report). Mitigation shipped: the test declares every kind that exists today with an exact error list, and the lock-in comment names the blind spot.

R2 A mis-move inside a transaction boundary would lose a rollback rather than crash one. Bounded by the unchanged suite, the canary, the -U0 diff showing only the eight guard lines removed, and the differential; the builder repeats those, not only the suite.

R3 The no-handle wording changes on paths that produced a typed result today ('was not identity-recorded', 'preserved replacement', bare 'rollback root is unavailable' become '<kind> left in place; rollback root is unavailable: <path>'). rg over the repo excluding *.go and do-work/ finds no consumer of the old strings; only prose in kb/ and the prime mentions 'preserved replacement' in another context.

R4 openRollbackRoot is package-level mutable state; a future test that sets it without t.Cleanup, or a t.Parallel added to the package, would leak the failure into other tests. Today the package cannot go parallel because newRepository uses t.Setenv.
R5 The shipped test's exact error and action lists couple it to the messages by design; a wording change must update the test in the same commit.

R6 Release bookkeeping is outside the write set: the commits change shipped files, so finalize owes the CHANGELOG.md entry and the byte-identical skills/do-work/CHANGELOG.md mirror; REQ-558 shipped two versions unnamed when this was missed.

R7 The gate on this machine is red for the two heavyverification tests regardless of this change; 'green' for step 5 means 'no new red', and the record must show the clean-HEAD pair beside the post-change run so that is checkable.

R8 Scratch state: I recreated scratchpad/req598 from a fresh clone (rm -rf first), so anything a sibling left there is gone; the sibling directories req598-gate, req598-decide-once, req598-ablate* were not touched. The builder works in its own worktree either way.
honest_downsides: It is a bigger change than the panic needs: +155/-81 in git_transaction.go plus a new 45-line Git-only walk inside a transaction boundary, for a path no user has reported, where a 7-line guard would have closed the panic. The payoff is structural: eight guards and a stale caller enumeration deleted, one decision point, honest no-handle messages, a pin at zero instead of a count, and a test that proves both halves of keep-going.

The shipped test does not drive a real OS failure; a seam stands in. The real condition (execute-only root, EACCES from os.OpenRoot while `git -C` works) was verified here only as uid 65534 in a throwaway probe; uid 0 opens such a root, which is where this suite runs, so that fixture is evidence in the record and not a test in the package.
The Git-only half duplicates the loop skeleton: no restore logic is copied (four shared helpers), but the kind-by-kind dispatch exists twice and must be edited twice.
One line of production code exists only for a test (the seam). The package already has that pattern (privateTransactionTestHook), which is the reason it is acceptable, not a reason it is free.

The no-handle path still reports committed_state_risk and leaves rooted targets as published, with no unrooted fallback; a user on a read-restricted worktree cleans up by hand, same as today, only now with a true list of what was left where.

The simplest shape of all, passing ExecuteTransaction's already-open line-467 handle into rollbackFailure and deleting the reopen, would remove the open, the seam and the whole no-handle half, but it makes the fixed requirement (a no-handle rollback test) unwritable and changes which directory object rollback acts on if the root is swapped mid-transaction. It was excluded by the requirement, not on merit; worth a line in the record for the maintainer.
The lock-in's Finding 3 block shrinks by 14 lines net but is a rewrite, not a renumber, so the reviewer reads the whole block again.

The widened test is 112 lines, one function, exact lists; it is the contract for rollbackWithoutRoot and that makes it long. Splitting it per kind would multiply the fixture six times for no extra failure named.

verdict.test_mechanism_verified:
Three mechanisms were run on this machine in a throwaway Go probe, as uid 0 and as uid 65534 via setpriv.
1. Execute-only root (chmod 0111): as uid 65534 os.OpenRoot fails with `open <dir>: permission denied` while `git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeds (the real condition, git alive); as uid 0 os.OpenRoot succeeds. A test on this mechanism skips at uid 0, which is where this session and its gate run, so neither plan ships it and neither should.
2. Rename the root away: os.OpenRoot fails with `open <dir>: no such file or directory` at both uids, and `git -C <dir>` fails with exit 128 at both uids. Real syscall failure, privilege-free, but the Git-side half of rollback is dead with it. Plan A's test on this mechanism: RED (panic at git_transaction.go:1213 root.Mkdir via rollbackFailure:1032 and ExecuteTransaction:586) with only the test applied on HEAD, PASS with A's guard, suite ok 2.434s, lock-in passed at 9; it also passes unchanged against B's source.

Seam (openRollbackRoot returning &os.PathError{Op: "open", Err: syscall.EACCES}): privilege-free, deterministic, git alive; the real os.OpenRoot PathError uses Op "open" (verified in GOROOT/src/os/root_unix.go openRootNolog and by observation), so the fabricated line mirrors a real one. Plan B's test and my widened six-kind test: RED at HEAD+seam (panic at root.Mkdir via rollbackFailure), PASS on B, PASS as uid 65534 from a compiled test binary, PASS under -race, windows vet clean. The seam is not a real OS failure and the record must say so; it is the only mechanism under which the keep-going claim (unstage happened, HEAD restore happened, exact error list) is assertable at uid 0.

verdict.what_the_losing_plan_had_right: Plan A was right that the guard belongs inside the consumer, not at the call site, because quarantineAndRollbackPrivate has two callers; right that the sibling message in rollbackDirtyTracked is bare and unattributable when several targets are declared (the differential shows the bare "rollback root is unavailable" with no path at HEAD); right that chmod 0111 skips at uid 0 and must not ship; right that a rename-away test needs no privileges and drives a real syscall failure, and its test does pass unchanged against B's source, so it was a sound test for its shape; right about the Windows caveat of renaming a directory with an open handle; right that the design smell remains under the ninth-guard shape and said so plainly; and right about the release obligation outside the write set. Its honest_downsides list was accurate on every point I checked, including that its shipped test could only prove the reporting half of keep-going. What it lacked was not care but a mechanism: with the root renamed away there is no way to assert the unstage half, and with nine per-consumer guards there is nothing in the code that makes a tenth consumer's missing guard visible.
